_README: Hand-verified retrieval test cases. Ground truth is a substring that a correctly
retrieved passage must contain - NOT a chunk ID, because chunk IDs change every
time the corpus is re-chunked, and these cases have to survive a parameter sweep.
question        - the query, phrased how a user would actually ask it
expect_any_of   - case-insensitive substrings; ANY match counts as a hit
(use several spellings - auto-captions mishear proper nouns)
city            - optional exact city filter to apply during retrieval
expect_no_match - true for negative cases: the corpus should NOT cover this,
and 'hit' means correctly returning nothing relevant
note            - why you know the ground truth; keep this honest
ADD MORE CASES. One case proves nothing - 15-30 spanning several cities,
question styles and difficulty levels is the minimum for tuning against.

cases.question: What events, fests or festivals did the city of Green Bay consider permits for?
cases.note: Verified by hand in the 3-22-21 Protection & Policy Committee transcript: a request to extend licensed premises to hold the fifth annual 'landusi fest'. Auto-captions render the club name inconsistently ('anduisi' / 'landusi'), hence two spellings. This case is currently a MISS - it is the failure that motivated the eval harness.

cases.question: landusi fest
cases.note: Same passage, but a short literal query instead of a natural question. Isolates whether compound phrasing is what breaks retrieval, or whether the passage is unreachable either way.

cases.question: Did an applicant request a waiver of the noise ordinance?
cases.note: Same meeting, different angle - the staff comment mentions the applicant asking for a noise ordinance waiver. Tests whether the surrounding discussion is reachable even when the event name isn't.

cases.question: How does a committee meeting begin - roll call and attendance?
cases.note: Easy positive control. Roll call appears in essentially every meeting; if this misses, something is broken at the pipeline level, not the ranking level.

cases.question: What did the council decide about the Mars colony landing site lease?
cases.note: Negative control: nothing in a Wisconsin council corpus should match. Passing means the retriever did not surface a spurious 'relevant' passage. Note that vector search always returns SOMETHING - this case checks the content, not the count.
